summary: Debut analysis video: DHFL bond sale panic drags housing finance stocks; speaker argues capitulation marks a bottom and irrational markets reward skilled traders.
lessons: Markets bottom after big panic selling (capitulation); overreaction to one name often marks a multi-week low.
Panic in one bond/stock drags the whole sector down with it - contagion is mechanical, not fundamental.
quotes: When people are optimistic they will pay the price of a diamond for a pebble; when pessimistic, they will not pay the price of a pebble for a diamond.

summary: VIX masterclass during COVID: definition (expected 30-day movement, not a fear gauge that must rise in falls), sqrt-12 monthly conversion, advance-decline check for why VIX fell on a falling day, and strike placement beyond the expected move.
lessons: VIX measures expected one-month movement; it can fall in a falling market when the fall is narrow (heavyweights only, breadth positive).
Monthly expected move = VIX / sqrt(12); place short strikes beyond that band (example: VIX 60 -> ~17% band).

strategies.name: VIX-based expected-move strangle placement
strategies.construction: Sell puts below spot - (VIX/sqrt(12))% and calls above spot + (VIX/sqrt(12))%
strategies.numbers: VIX 60 -> monthly band ~17.3%; spot 8,000 -> sell puts below ~6,500, calls above ~9,500; May 8,000 straddle ~1,600 (~20% for 37 trading days)
strategies.best_regime: Elevated VIX (crisis); recompute daily as VIX moves
strategies.adjustments: None stated - guideline framing, refresh band as VIX changes
strategies.risks: Band is statistical, not a wall; theta/other factors shift premiums; violent moves can exceed the band

quotes: It is not necessary that when the market goes down, the VIX has to go up - VIX is all about the perception of the market over the next one month.

summary: First-ever Week Ahead video: 3-session COVID holiday week; India VIX falling; Friday's terrible US jobs data moved Dow only -300 (selling exhaustion); HDFC/ICICI ADRs -8% warn of weak Tuesday open; range 7,500-8,500.
lessons: When bad news moves markets less and less, selling is exhausting - negative impact is limited.
ADR moves of index heavyweights preview Indian bank stocks after holidays.

summary: Against unanimous retail bearishness in COVID: lead-vs-lag indicators, the good/very-good/bad/very-bad news quadrant, consensus danger, efficient markets ('you are last to know'), and why heavy put buying at high premium is a losing game.
lessons: Markets price the lead indicator (next few months) - current bad news is already in the price (efficient market: you are last to know).
Very good news invites profit booking; very bad news invites policy rescue - so both can be sell/buy signals respectively.
quotes: Good news is a good news; very good news is a bad news. Bad news is a bad news; very bad news is a good news.

summary: P&L transparency episode: ~50% return in six April-2020 sessions driven by VIX collapse 86->50 plus a bullish view; demonstrates position-level losses coexisting with net profit, and strike/expiry diversification; explicitly warns viewers not to copy the risk.
lessons: High-VIX regimes let low-volume sellers earn outsized returns as VIX collapses - the profit engine is vega plus view, not volume.
Spread risk across many strikes (6,500 through 8,500 puts) and multiple expiries (weekly/May/June) - never concentrate one strike.

strategies.name: Strike-and-expiry put ladder (illustrative, high risk)
strategies.construction: Sold puts at 6,500 / 7,000 / 7,300 / 7,400 / 7,500 / 7,800 / 8,500 across weekly, May and June expiries; small stock-option positions (IndusInd 800 qty @22.52; ~2,300PE on a NBFC stock, 4 lots @220)
strategies.numbers: Capital ~95 lakh -> ~45 lakh profit in 6 sessions (~50%); sold Jun 7,000PE @475, May 6,500PE @210 (closed 80), May 7,000PE @324 (closed 117)
strategies.best_regime: Extreme high VIX with stabilizing market (COVID April 2020)
strategies.adjustments: Laddered entries across expiries instead of single-strike concentration
strategies.risks: Aggressive directional sizing; a renewed crash through the ladder strikes would produce large losses; explicitly not replicable by retail

quotes: We also lose. What matters is whether, at the end of the day, the profits are more than the losses.

summary: PM announced a further 19-day lockdown. Argues the move was 90% expected, so already priced; SGX Nifty traded ~200 points above the India close; herd put-buyers set up for a premium collapse even if prices fell.
lessons: Markets can absorb good or bad news but not uncertainty; once an outcome is known, clarity itself re-prices risk.
When 90% expect a fall, the fall is already priced - consensus trades usually fail.

strategies.name: Multi-strike, multi-expiry put selling (April 2020)
strategies.construction: Sold put options spread across various strike prices and expiry periods rather than one strike
strategies.numbers: 7500PE sold around Rs.75 during a morning dip; SGX Nifty ~9200 vs ~9000 close
strategies.best_regime: Ultra-bearish consensus with the negative surprise already announced
strategies.adjustments: Exited or rolled by expiry; profit disclosed in a later review video
strategies.risks: Losses if the market breaks below the sold strikes; premium is the cap on profit

quotes: Markets can take good news, markets can take bad news, but markets just cannot take the uncertainty.

summary: Historical framing of gold: price fixed by UK for a century, market data from 1973; three spikes - 1980 Iran revolution/oil crisis, 2008 Lehman, 2020 COVID. Logic: global crisis forces rate cuts, money exits deposits into gold.
lessons: Gold spikes when a global crisis forces central banks to slash rates - near-zero deposit rates make yieldless gold attractive.
Whether to buy gold depends on your view of how long the crisis and the low-rate regime will last.
quotes: Whenever there is a problem faced by the entire world, the gold prices will shoot up.

summary: Explains the historic negative WTI print: contracts marked for physical delivery with storage full forced holders to pay to exit, driving May-2020 futures to -$37 while June contracts stayed normal. Analogy-driven, with explicit disclaimers.
lessons: Contracts expiring into physical delivery can print absurd prices when storage is exhausted - know delivery mechanics before holding.
Negative prices were contract-specific: the next-month contract kept trading at normal positive levels.
quotes: Storage facilities are completely full, no more storage is possible, and that created a huge panic among the buyers.

summary: Builds the case that expert stock-picking barely beats chance: hundreds of coexisting technical methods cannot all work; Malkiel's blindfolded-monkey argument; WSJ dartboard contest (61% expert pick wins, only 51% beat the Dow); 2018 rerun where dart picks returned 17.3% vs experts -4.4% vs S&P +11%.
lessons: If hundreds of technical methods coexist, most cannot work - treat technical analysis as one input, never the system.
In the WSJ decade-long dartboard contest, pros beat the darts 61% of the time but beat the Dow only 51% of the time.
quotes: Technical analysis is part of the trading system, not the heart of the trading system.

summary: Two case studies where technicians were trapped: RBI's May 2018 FII window opening in HDFC Bank (cash-futures arb by funds crushed late buyers) and the 2011 flash crash from a broker's basket-order error (Nifty -15% intraday, futures only -3-4%). Conclusion: no single system works.
lessons: Look at everything - news, flows, regulation - never one indicator alone
When a known buying window opens, front-runners buy in cash and short futures; late chart-followers get trapped
quotes: No particular system works in the stock market. If any one system worked, everybody would be following that.

summary: Argues index options beat stock options: indices cannot crash 50-60% in a day (DHFL -65%, Infibeam -70% did), index margins are half of stock margins for similar contract size, far-strike liquidity is deep, no physical delivery, panic exits always available.
lessons: Return on margin matters, not how much the underlying moves - index gives 6-7% on margin vs 4% for a stock moving twice as much
Stocks can gap 50-70% overnight; indices are circuit-protected
quotes: At the end of the day, what matters is the return on our investment. It is not how many percent the underlying moves.

summary: Monthly P&L review: April profit 66.3 lakh on ~95 lakh starting capital after 45 lakh in first two weeks; attributes windfall to India VIX collapse 80-85 to ~40 and Nifty clearing the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement (9300-9400) toward 9900-10000; March also +50 lakh selling calls.
lessons: High collapsing VIX plus a clear directional view is where option sellers make windfall profits - not repeatable monthly
Know when to exit: he closed nearly all positions after the Fibonacci target hit

strategies.name: Put-selling ladder in collapsing-VIX rebound
strategies.construction: Sold puts across strikes from ~6,100 to 9,000 during April 2020 recovery
strategies.numbers: April profit 66,30,478 on ~95L capital; VIX 80-85 -> 55-60 -> ~40; June 9000PE sold at 500, closed 180
strategies.best_regime: post-crash VIX collapse with market refusing to make new lows
strategies.risks: windfall not repeatable; VIX normalizes; requires conviction view

quotes: A trader can make profit even in a falling market and lose money even in a rising market - it is the view of the trader that is more important.

summary: April series ended near highs (~9,850) but weekend brought lockdown extension and zero April auto sales; SGX indicated 500-650 point gap down (worst since March); monthly OI range 9,000-10,500; 10,000 major resistance (Fib 50%).
lessons: May is historically a weak month for equities ('Sell in May') - factor seasonality into OI positioning.
Known-bad data (zero auto sales) is priced in; markets react to surprises, not confirmations.

summary: Two-year Reliance thesis: refinery scale and superior GRMs plus the Jio pivot from commodity to telecom/retail argue for a PE re-rating from ~25 toward 40-50, implying Rs 2,500-3,000; documents the Jio stake-sale wave and the Rs 1,257 rights issue; buy on fundamentals, time on technicals, or use cash-secured puts/SIP.
lessons: Commodity businesses get PE ~10-11; telecom/retail get 40-150+ - business-mix change drives re-rating more than earnings alone.
Choose WHAT to buy from fundamentals; choose WHEN from technicals, cash-secured puts, or SIP.
quotes: The biggest risk in your life is not taking any risk.

summary: Century-scale argument against crash calls: 100 years of Dow history shows every major crash (1929 ~90%, dot-com, Lehman) was followed by a powerful rebound; India's 1992/2000/2008/2020 parallels; Nifty PE ~16 sits in the historical buy zone (15-16) vs 28-30 sell zone; advises staggered ETF investing and cash-secured puts; '7500 bottom already made'.
lessons: Markets are unpredictable short-term but mean-revert upward across decades - every crash has been the entry for the next bull.
PE 15-16 has historically been an accumulation zone; 28-30 a distribution zone for Indian indices.

strategies.name: Staggered index investing with cash-secured puts
strategies.construction: SIP into a Nifty 50 ETF; optionally place cash-secured puts at desired lower entries
strategies.numbers: Nifty PE ~16 (May 2020); historical buy zone 15-16, sell zone 28-30; Dow 1929 crash ~90%; 1982-2000 bull ~15x

quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: Explains donation-tax mechanics using his charity webinar: PM/CM fund donations get 100% exemption but are capped at 10% of annual profit unless a special COVID ordinance removed the cap for PM Cares; NGO donations only 50%, still 10%-capped; net effect was an extra ~Rs 1.5 lakh personal outflow - 'tax saving is a myth'.
lessons: Donation exemptions cannot shelter trading income: 100% exemption applies only within the 10%-of-profit cap (except the PM Cares ordinance window).
Donations to approved PM/CM funds: 100% deduction; most NGOs: 50% deduction - both subject to the qualifying-limit rule.

summary: Q&A clarifying mechanics: buy/sell quantities are always equal (TV 'delivery buying' is interpretation); futures settle daily via MTM while option sellers' margin = span + premium value, rising with the option price; NSE uses a 10% risk-free rate in IV; June-2020 hedged margins ~one-third of naked; expiry settlement uses last-half-hour weighted average, not last traded price.
lessons: Futures: daily MTM cash transfer. Options: buyer pays premium once; seller's margin floats with the option's price.
Expiry settlement price is the weighted average of the last half hour - an ITM option can expire worthless despite a favorable last traded price.

summary: Market reaction to the Atmanirbhar package: Nifty broke the key 9,000 support as FIIs sold over Rs 4,000 crore in two sessions; argues the package repackaged earlier announcements with under ~Rs 2 lakh crore true cash outlay and no tax/GST/corporate relief unlike the 2013 playbook; keeps only the market-facts, drops political commentary.
lessons: Announced headline stimulus and actual cash outlay can differ by an order of magnitude - trade the market's verdict, not the headline.
A break of a psychologically important round-number support after a disappointment signals continuation, not opportunity.

summary: Explains the 8,950PE flash spike (0.50 to ~20 in minutes) as a probable fat-finger market buy, citing the earlier NSE episode where a broker's basket-order error crashed Nifty ~15% before reversal; notes May's three weekly expiries all closed within 9,100-9,200 despite violent daily swings; then unpacks why Reliance's rights entitlement traded 30-40 above intrinsic (staggered 25/25/50 payment schedule).
lessons: Resting limit orders far from spot can get filled by flash spikes; square off immediately - such dislocations vanish in seconds and cannot be systematically captured.
A month can be violently volatile intraday yet flat close-to-close: distance-based option selling harvests the chaos.
quotes: Sometimes the market is like a beach horse: it runs around, but always returns to the same spot.

summary: Explains Bharat Bond: a debt ETF holding only PSU bonds maturing before scheme maturity; 0.0005% expense (cheapest in India), 3-year and 10-year maturities, ~6.8%/7.6% indicative yields, 20% LTCG with indexation after 3 years, 5% collateral haircut, exchange-listed liquidity.
lessons: Falling interest-rate environments lift long-duration bond ETF prices - match duration to the rate view.
A 0.0005% expense ratio compounds into materially higher post-tax yield versus active debt funds.

strategies.name: Bharat Bond as trading collateral
strategies.construction: Buy Bharat Bond ETF units; pledge to broker as collateral for F&O margins
strategies.numbers: ~7.6% indicative 10yr yield; 20% LTCG with indexation >3yr; 5% haircut; EBBETF 0423 ~1019, EBBETF 0430 ~1050 (May 2020)
strategies.best_regime: declining interest rates; idle capital awaiting trade opportunities
strategies.risks: rising rates compress price; credit concentration in PSU issuers

quotes: If interest rates in the economy go lower, these bonds will do very well; the day rates start rising, the premium will not look good.

summary: Monthly trade review: ~10 lakh May profit on ~95 lakh capital (76 lakh total in two months, ~80%). Dissects three large losses (Nifty future and two call options, ~12 lakh combined), a profitable ratio spread, cash-secured puts in ICICI/HDFC Bank, and corrects an earlier mistaken March figure.
lessons: Never benchmark one month against the last - the market 'is like God; take what it gives'. Expectation inflation destroys discipline.
Index-only trading survives regime changes: when SEBI raised stock-option margins from June 2020, index positions kept the margin edge.

strategies.name: Cash-secured puts (ICICI 300PE, HDFC 840PE)
strategies.construction: Sell puts below market with full cash set aside for delivery
strategies.best_regime: moderately bullish with stocks near support
strategies.adjustments: take delivery if assigned; roll if view changes
strategies.risks: sharp breakdown below strike forces delivery at loss

quotes: People lose money because they do not want to lose money - they expect zero-loss calls, which is impossible.

summary: Tax primer: cash-market gains taxed at 15% STCG / 10% LTCG above 1 lakh (post-2018), while F&O profits are business income taxed at slab rates with full expense deduction. Compares individual vs corporate accounts: ~42% top personal rate vs 22-25% corporate, but MAT ~18% limits corporate loss set-off.
lessons: F&O income is business income: slab rates hurt, but expense deduction (broadband, office, salaries, depreciation) and loss set-off often win.
Individual accounts can carry trading losses forward ~8 years against future profits; corporate accounts face MAT (~18%) even in profit years, limiting set-off value.
quotes: Go and make profit first, then come to me - the auditor's answer to every F&O tax question.

summary: Bullish call vindicated: Nifty 9,000->10,200 in ~7 sessions as FIIs turned daily buyers; US May payrolls +2.5M vs -8M expected sent Nasdaq to ATH; recounts Nov-2018 elections->Balakot FII cycle; NSE option-price glitch Thursday hurt traders.
lessons: Don't be a bull or a bear - be a chameleon; markets change trend when everyone leans one way.
Always trade with the trend; fighting it with leverage (F&O) makes losses heavy.

summary: Euphoric gap-up morning (Nifty +200, Bank Nifty +500) fizzled: pre-market blog call that Nifty future would break 10,200 at least once played out; session closed as a Doji via the weighted-average close; RBI nod for IndusInd open-market buys lifted it early while HDFC/Kotak/Reliance were sold hard from highs; FII +813 cr vs DII -1,238 cr; view: consolidation with positive bias, supports 9,900/9,700.
lessons: Euphoric gaps attract profit-booking: 'a bull market dies of euphoria' - fade the open, respect the close.
The printed close is a last-half-hour weighted average - comparing it to yesterday's true close can fake a 'Doji' or fake momentum.
quotes: A bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: US reality-check week: Nasdaq ATH despite 2M+ infections; Fed caution sent US -7% Thursday; Nifty closed ~10,000 Friday instead of feared crash (already -2% Thursday; Asia only -1-2%); IIP -55% (lockdown); consolidation 9,500-10,500.
lessons: Relative positioning logic: if you already fell 2% and Asia only falls 1-2% after a US -7% night, the gap-down gets bought.
Already-corrected markets have less downside from a global shock - fresh shorting invites short covering.

summary: Builds a limited-risk call ratio on the post-COVID rally: buy 1x 10,500 Aug CE @360, sell 3x 11,000 Aug CE, buy 2x 11,500 Aug CE; net credit ~1,900; margin ~63,000 effective; max profit ~37,000 at Nifty 11,000; breakeven 11,253; max loss ~37,000 above 11,500; anchored on 200-DMA + 50% Fibonacci resistance.
lessons: Turn a 'resistance holds' view into a credit ratio spread; add far calls to cap the unlimited-risk tail.
Net-credit gating: if the structure is a debit in the near expiry, step out to the far month where it pays you.

strategies.name: Limited-risk call ratio spread (1:3:2)
strategies.construction: Buy 1x 10,500 CE (Aug), sell 3x 11,000 CE (Aug), buy 2x 11,500 CE (Aug)
strategies.numbers: Net credit ~Rs 1,900; margin ~Rs 65,000 (Rs 63,000 effective); max profit ~Rs 37,000 at Nifty 11,000; upper breakeven 11,253; max loss ~Rs 37,000 above 11,500
strategies.best_regime: After a sharp rally, into strong resistance (200-DMA + 50% retracement of 12,400->7,500)
strategies.adjustments: Exit all legs together; partial exit leaves naked short calls
strategies.risks: Sustained breakout above 11,500 hits max loss; requires two-month view

summary: Q&A: blue-chip etymology from casino chips; SLB as delivery backstop; American vs European styles and assignment risk; no exchange-resident stop-loss for delivery trades in India; breakeven limits unknowable pre-expiry; long-term patience (Reliance flat 2008-17, then 3.5x); discretionary trading produced best and worst single days (±10% of capital).
lessons: 'Blue chip' comes from the casino's highest-value chip - the term predates markets.
No exchange-held stop-loss for delivery positions in India; brokers simulate GTC by re-placing daily.
quotes: Equity needs patience: some stocks give ten years of return in the last two years.

summary: Post-rally consolidation view: support 9,900, resistance 10,700; Fed restricted bank buybacks (Dow -700 Friday); ITC results in line; data week ahead (auto sales, China/India PMI, US payrolls Thursday).
lessons: After a 1,000-point monthly rally, expect 1-2 weeks of range consolidation, not continuation.
Central-bank restrictions on one sector (bank buybacks) can drag the whole US tape overnight.

summary: Reconciles a Reliance long-futures position: June 2020 rally from 1460 to 1784 gave ~3 lakh stock profit, but total P&L of 592,592 (as of Friday) came from an options overlay - sold-call ladders plus a straddle conversion. An error trade (call sold instead of put) forced doubled corrective legs and ~30 adjustment trades.
lessons: Hedging a directional position with short calls can outperform the stock itself - profit doubled versus holding the future alone.
One mis-executed leg (call instead of put) forced doubling of offsetting legs and heavy margin strain - verify every leg at entry.

strategies.name: Hedged long stock/futures with call ladder + straddle conversion
strategies.construction: Long 2 lots (1000 shares) Reliance futures from ~1010; sold 1580/1600/1640/1680/1700 calls progressively; converted a 1500 short call into a short straddle by selling 1500 puts (later doubled after error)
strategies.numbers: June: stock +~3,00,000; options overlay +~2,90,000; total 592,592 at month-end week; ~30 trades executed
strategies.best_regime: Strongly trending large-cap you want to hold; sell calls above trend to monetize drift
strategies.adjustments: Rolled sold calls up the ladder as price ran; doubled puts after leg error; kept net long exposure
strategies.risks: Gap above highest sold call caps upside; margin spikes when doubling corrective legs

quotes: if the market goes down, we make money in call options... the idea is to outperform the stock itself

summary: Q&A batch: no fixed monthly returns as an option seller (HNI pattern: FD/debt-fund collateral is the primary income, trading is a bonus); margin shortfall penalty slabs; no safe strategy and no permanently strong company; minimum capital views; index fund vs futures; physical-delivery discipline; arbitrage vs reverse arbitrage on discounted futures.
lessons: Anchor option-selling expectations to collateral yield: primary income is interest on pledged debt funds; trading profit is supplementary and irregular.
Margin shortfall penalty: 0.5% of shortfall below 1 lakh, 1% above it, rising to 5% if the breach repeats beyond five sessions - never overtrade your collateral.

strategies.name: Collateral-funded option selling (HNI pattern)
strategies.construction: Pledge debt mutual funds/bank FDs as collateral; sell options against the margin; keep interest as primary return
strategies.numbers: Stated pattern: 6-7% interest on debt funds while trading on pledged limit
strategies.best_regime: Wealthy, income-focused sellers who accept trading as a bonus stream
strategies.risks: Trading losses eat the collateral cushion; interest is not guaranteed against credit events

quotes: stock market is not for the people who are expecting a regular or fixed return

summary: US jobs beats lifted Nifty to a 4-month high ~10,605; volatility regime shift - India VIX 30->25 and Friday's range <100 points (first in months); +55 points but calls didn't gain even 1 rupee; OI range 10,000-11,000.
lessons: Falling VIX crushes premiums even on up days - option sellers win in quiet drifts.
OI map (max put 10,000, max call 11,000) with >90 premiums frames a clean range to sell around.

summary: Market recap (HDFC Bank deposit-growth gap-up, Reliance+HDFC Bank over half the Nifty rally, FIIs and DIIs both net buyers) plus a clean explainer: extraordinary dividends (>5% of market value) trigger option strike adjustments on ex-date - ITC's 10-rupee dividend reset strikes; brokers cannot change strikes at will. Dividend-capture via cash buy + futures short pocketed ~5% in days.
lessons: When a dividend exceeds 5% of market value, exchanges adjust option strikes (and premiums) on ex-date - the broker did not change anything; check corporate actions before trading stock options.
Ex-dividend drops create a short-lived arbitrage: buy cash, short futures, collect the dividend, square both at convergence.

strategies.name: Dividend capture via cash-futures arbitrage
strategies.construction: Buy stock in cash market before ex-date; short equal futures; collect dividend; square both legs post ex-date
strategies.numbers: ITC dividend >10 rupees on a ~200 rupee stock; ~5% return in days as stated
strategies.best_regime: Extraordinary dividends (>5% of market value) where futures still price the gross dividend
strategies.risks: Futures may already price the dividend; margin on short futures; execution costs

quotes: whenever a company declares a dividend more than 5% of the market value... option prices will be adjusted

summary: Q&A batch: STT mechanics on sellers; time decay proportional to expiry (weekly day-1 = 20% of decay, expiry day = 100%); covered calls against physical shares still need full margin in India (no cash-F&O link) but a long futures leg reduces it to exposure margin; Bharat Bond 1 vs 2 (yield, premium, pledge-ability delay); NSE's six-month co-location ban on new contracts had just ended; bear/bull defined by 20% thresholds.
lessons: Time decay is proportional to remaining time: a one-week option loses ~20% of its value on day one, but ~100% on expiry day - expiry-day selling harvests decay that weekly sellers spread across days.
India charges full span+exposure margin on covered calls against demat shares (no cash-F&O link); holding a long future instead cuts the short call's span to zero - only exposure margin applies.

strategies.name: Covered call via futures leg (margin-optimized)
strategies.construction: Hold long futures instead of physical shares; sell calls against it
strategies.numbers: Stated: span margin zero for the covered call against long futures; exposure margin ~2% index, ~3.5% stock options
strategies.best_regime: Large holders wanting option income without physical-settlement complexity
strategies.adjustments: Roll calls up as futures rally
strategies.risks: Futures MTM swings; margin calls if exposure margin rules change

quotes: when running a casino is more profitable, why do people choose to be gamblers?

summary: Counters technical analysts calling for a 7500 retest: after the October 2008 Lehman low (2252), Nifty doubled within a year and the low was never retested; the COVID candle's high was 11400 - once crossed, it may never be retested. COVID fell less than 50% (vs 2008's >50%), so recovery may be slower, but 15000 arrives before 7500. Investment timing: invest when you have surplus cash; exit when you need the money.
lessons: Post-crash lows of true panic candles (2008, 2020) are historically not retested once the recovery candle's high is crossed - drawdown bottoming behaves asymmetrically.
The depth of the crash sets the pace of recovery: 2008's >50% fall doubled in a year; 2020's shallower fall implies a slower but persistent recovery.
quotes: the right time to invest is when you have surplus cash. The right time to exit is when you need the money

summary: Counters the 'invest for long term' reflex: Nifty top-50 averaged ~11x over 1994-2020 (doubling slower than 6 years) while risk-free debt doubled in ~6; only stock-pickers or entry-exit timers should invest; Anil Ambani group stocks lost 95-99%.
lessons: Nifty top-50 average return 1994-2020 did not double in 6 years, underperforming risk-free debt instruments doubling in ~6.
Index survivorship inflates returns: failing companies are ejected, so you average only the winning horses.
quotes: Stock market is only for two people: those who can pick the stock that performs, or those who know when to get in and out.

summary: Defends the 15000-before-7500 call: consensus is dangerous (99% polled bearish, market rallied); Nifty PE 28 is not a fixed top because Rule-of-72 FD doubling moved 9->18 years, tripling justifiable PE; dividend-yield screen says market is skeptical, not euphoric.
lessons: Consensus is dangerous: when 99% expect a fall, markets climb the wall of worry.
Justifiable PE scales inversely with interest rates - with FD doubling in 18 years (4%), a 3x premium implies PE far above the historic 28 top.
quotes: Bull market is born out of pessimism, grows out of skepticism, matures out of optimism and dies out of euphoria.

summary: P&L showcase: claims Rs 1.05 cr profit April-July 2020 on Rs 95 L capital (~110% in 4 months), Rs 66L April / Rs 10L May / -Rs 1.2L June / Rs 31L July; also claims Rs 47L profit during the March 2020 crash and Rs 1.55 cr over 10 months; closes with troll-defense and workshop-review promotion.
lessons: Option selling is a book of many trades: a few failures drown in the aggregate profit - the insurance-pool principle.
Adjustments and firefighting (not stop-losses) are how a losing view becomes a small profit or small loss.
quotes: I am not the god, I am just good.

summary: Selling from two stocks: Reliance -120 from highs (16% Nifty weight) and HDFC Bank on Aditya Puri's ~850 crore share sale (-100 rupees = -1,000 Bank Nifty points); Apple overtook Saudi Aramco Friday night; RBI policy Thursday; narrow ~500-point range, VIX ~24.
lessons: A heavyweight insider sale can cost the index 1,000 points on one stock - weightage math matters.
Low VIX (~24) = narrow-range regime; position size for ~500-point weeks, not crash weeks.

summary: Explains SEBI's cash-market margin changes effective 1 August 2020: upfront margin now required even to sell shares already held, because the exchange cannot distinguish intraday sells from delivery sells. Walks through VaR+ELM+additional margin arithmetic (Reliance ~22%, SBI ~35%, Idea ~77.5%), T+2 settlement, early pay-in, and the auction market for short deliveries; predicts movement toward T+1.
lessons: Intraday margin scales with stock volatility: roughly 4.5x leverage on Reliance (~22%) but barely 1.3x on Idea (~77.5%) at the time.
From August 2020, selling shares you already hold also requires margin in the account - the exchange cannot tell an intraday sell from a delivery sell.
quotes: Anything that cannot be liquidated immediately cannot be given as a collateral.

summary: Reliance long-futures case study: entry ~1400 (May 2020), price ~2000 by 3 August 2020. Pure cash-market hold would have made ~6 lakh; dynamic hedging and firefighting made ~13.1 lakh in the main account plus 8 lakh+ in a second account (~21-22 lakh total), though 40-50 lakh extra margin was injected. Detailed adjustment ladder: sold 1800/1900/2000 calls, rolled to 2040/2100, sold 2180 call, bought 1700 put (over 1 lakh loss), sold puts 1680 down to 1400, then aggressively sold 1900-2200 puts (12.66 lakh from put selling in July).
lessons: A hedged directional position can triple a plain cash-market gain (6L -> ~21-22L) - but only with margin headroom (40-50L extra injected here).
Firefighting ladder on a runaway trend: sell calls above, roll them up as the trend extends, then fund the ride by selling puts below the market.

strategies.name: Reliance long futures + rolling option ladder
strategies.construction: Long 2 lots futures (~1000 shares @~1400); short 1800/1900/2000CE rolled to 2040/2100CE then 2180CE; long 1700PE; short 1680/1640/1600/1500/1400PE; later aggressive short 1900-2200PE
strategies.numbers: 13.12L profit (main account, incl. 12.66L from July put selling + 84k August); ~8L+ second account; ~40-50L additional margin deployed
strategies.best_regime: Strong vertical uptrend with high IV ( premium selling on both sides)
strategies.adjustments: Roll short calls up strike by strike; convert to put selling below market once trend confirmed; accept small hedge losses
strategies.risks: Deep gap reversal against both legs; escalating margin needs; overconfidence after wins

quotes: Many people think you have to trade too much to make profit, but here I traded only two lots.

summary: Q&A episode: expiry-day mechanics for hedged shorts (removing the long leg makes the short naked; index options cash-settle, stock options physically deliver if ITM - square off yourself); F&O ban-list illiquidity; advice to avoid stock F&O below ~1 crore capital and prefer indices; collateral eligibility (REC bonds, property, ELSS under 3 years ineligible); 50% cash margin component rule; Bharat Bond is cumulative, not annual-pay; option selling not advisable below ~10 lakh capital; no fixed timeline to become a successful trader.
lessons: Removing the protective long leg on expiry day converts your short into a naked position - margin and risk jump; close positions yourself rather than letting settlement decide.
Physical delivery applies only to stock F&O: short ITM call = give delivery, short ITM put = take delivery. Indices are cash-settled.
quotes: Anything that cannot be liquidated immediately cannot be given as a collateral.

summary: Critique of SEBI's peak-margin framework: intraday leverage phased out (from Dec 1 2020, brokers could offer only ~3x, then 1x, then ~0.25x, ultimately none by around August-September 2021); margin must cover peak intraday MTM exposure, penalized 0.5%/1% per day on shortages. Highlights unfairness of freak trades (a single 10,800 print vs 11,000 Nifty) creating phantom MTM losses, and argues SEBI restricts option sellers while the real speculators are option buyers - the drunkard-searching-under-the-streetlight analogy.
lessons: Peak-margin logic: your account must fund the worst intraday MTM excursion, not just the closing position - violent days create penalty risk even if the day ends flat.
The phase-out calendar (Dec 2020: ~3x intraday limit; +3 months: ~1x; +3 months: ~0.25x; by Aug-Sep 2021: none) forced the end of 10x-100x broker leverage.
quotes: Sometimes SEBI behaves like the man who lost his ring in the dark but searches under the streetlight because the light is there.

summary: Gold crashed 6% in a day (silver -15%) days after Russia's COVID-vaccine announcement, from its ~$2,070 all-time high. Historical frame: gold's three modern spikes (1980 oil crisis $200->$600+, 2008 Lehman $700->$1900, 2020 COVID $1200->$2000+) all came with global crises and collapsing rates; the 2011 peak was followed by a one-day 10% crash and a slide to $1070. Argues $2070 will not be revisited until the next systemic crisis; notes rotation from new-economy to old-economy stocks, and that markets rise when everybody is bearish. Personal book: 60-70 lakh in December 2020 index options gaining ~1 lakh/day for three days (+3%) as IV fell 30->20; buy 400-500 point Nifty dips.
lessons: Gold's modern spikes map to global crises (1980 oil shock, 2008 Lehman, 2020 COVID) - it is a fear asset, not a return asset.
Gold's all-time highs get made during systemic crises and can take decades to revisit (1980 peak held until 2008; post-2011 high ran to $1070).

strategies.name: Long-dated index option buying on IV collapse
strategies.construction: Deployed 60-70 lakh across December 2020 Nifty options (puts and calls), holding 30-40 lakh cash for adjustments
strategies.numbers: +~1 lakh/day for three consecutive days (~3% on deployed capital) as IV fell from ~30 to ~20
strategies.best_regime: Post-panic IV compression with market stabilization
strategies.risks: Time decay if IV stays low and market ranges; long options bleed without direction

quotes: When the whole world is facing a big problem, that is when the gold prices will shoot up.

summary: ADR explainer anchored on ICICI Bank's 10 August 2020 QIP: targeted 15,000 crore, drew ~62,000 crore (4x+ oversubscribed); the ADR rose ~4% overnight, so Bank Nifty puts were sold next morning for profit. Explains ADR mechanics and ratios (HDFC Bank ADR = 3 shares, ICICI = 2, Tata Motors = 4, Vedanta = 5), why HDFC Bank's ADR traded ~10% premium (FII ownership limit exhausted, so US buyers pay up rather than hit the India cap), and notes GDRs in London (Reliance).
lessons: ADR overnight moves are a reliable next-day read-through for most large caps - the same global holders reprice the Indian line at open.
ADR ratios vary (1 ADR = 2-5 Indian shares); convert properly before comparing prices.
quotes: ADRs are the Indian shares which are being traded in US stock exchanges.

summary: Mechanics of the F&O ban (Market Wide Position Limit): MWPL = 20% of free-float market cap; a stock enters ban when combined open interest ends a day above 95% of MWPL; no fresh F&O positions next day (existing positions square-off only); ban lifts only when OI falls below 80%. Penalty for banned trading: 1% of contract value or 5,000 rupees, whichever is higher, capped at 1 lakh/day. Live examples: Vodafone Idea at 93.5% utilization, Canara Bank in ban at 88.5% (descending), Adani Enterprises at 88% not banned; nine stocks in ban for 12 August 2020.
lessons: MWPL math: 20% of free-float market cap caps total F&O open interest; speculative smallcaps hit it far sooner than large caps.
Ban asymmetry: entry at 95% utilization but exit only below 80% - ban lists persist for days and freeze hedgers mid-position.
quotes: Usually the stocks that come under trading ban are the highly speculative stocks.

summary: Pair trading as a market-neutral structure: long one instrument, short another (often same sector, e.g., long HDFC/ICICI vs short SBI/BoB; long Maruti vs short Tata Motors). COVID example: Maruti -33% while Tata Motors -85% made the pair hugely profitable. Live demonstration with Nifty long / Bank Nifty short across one week, two weeks and one month (Aug 2020) showing positive net P&L in all three windows as Nifty outperformed (10,200 -> ~11,300 while Bank Nifty crawled 21,500 -> 21,800).
lessons: Pair trading isolates relative strength: you profit from the spread between two instruments, not from market direction - gaps and crashes largely cancel.
Classic pairs: private banks long vs PSU banks short; quality autos long vs weak autos short; index long vs lagging index short.

strategies.name: Nifty long / Bank Nifty short pair
strategies.construction: Long 1 lot Nifty futures + short 1 lot Bank Nifty futures (25 lot size), rebalanced views weekly
strategies.numbers: One-week window: ~4,725 loss on Nifty leg vs ~12,775 profit on Bank Nifty leg; two-week window: net ~12,000+ profit; one-month window positive
strategies.best_regime: Index divergence phases - Bank Nifty underperforming Nifty for weeks
strategies.adjustments: Re-evaluate pair weekly; exit when the spread normalizes
strategies.risks: Correlation breakdown in crashes; both legs can lose if sized wrong; margin on two futures legs

quotes: Pair trading means going long in one stock and going short in another - the differential profit is your profit.

summary: Follow-up on the ITC call (bought ~198, now ~170, -15%): thesis unchanged - dividend yield above FD rates, effective cost cut below 170 by selling calls, patience and averaging down; high-dividend stocks are income plays, not momentum plays. New pick: BPCL - corrected from ~450-460 to ~350 on divestment delay; dividend yield ~4.65%; OMC earnings inversely track crude, and CME curves price crude flat (~$40-43) out to Dec 2022 and beyond. Entry paths: cash-secured puts (sold 350PE @14) or covered calls; full disclaimer.
lessons: Dividend-yield investing is a patience game: price declines raise the yield and attract institutions - the thesis strengthens as the price falls (if the dividend sustains).
Selling covered calls against a stock position lowers effective cost (bought ~198, effective <170) - income cushions drawdowns in non-momentum stocks.

strategies.construction: Sold BPCL 350PE at ~14 (August 2020 expiry), cash reserved for assignment
strategies.best_regime: Stock corrected on event delay; willing to own at strike
strategies.adjustments: Roll or take delivery and switch to covered calls
strategies.risks: Assignment in extended divestment delay / crude spike

quotes: The more the price goes down, the more the dividend yield - and more institutions will show interest.

summary: Introduces MCX BULLDEX bullion-index futures launched 24 Aug 2020: 70.52% gold / 29.48% silver weights, lot 50, monthly expiry, price ~16,000, contract ~8 lakh, margin ~6% (~48,000), tick 1. Frames gold as an inverse-correlation hedge and a pair-trading complement to equity positions.
lessons: Gold moves opposite equities over long cycles - 2008-2011 gold rose >400% post-Lehman while stocks crashed; 2020 COVID gold nearly doubled from the bottom.
A 10-20% bullion exposure lets equity shorts/longs be paired against gold positions as a cross-asset hedge.

strategies.construction: Long/short equity portfolio paired with same-direction or inverse position in MCX BULLDEX futures (70.52% gold / 29.48% silver)
strategies.numbers: lot 50; ~16,000 index; ~8 lakh contract value; ~6% margin (~48,000); tick 1
strategies.best_regime: Portfolio-level diversification when equity-gold inverse correlation is intact
strategies.adjustments: Rebalance weights as gold/silver ratio drifts; roll monthly expiry

quotes: When the markets are in bull mode, the gold will be in a bear mode. When the markets are in bear mode, the gold will be in a bull mode.

summary: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das said markets are disconnected from reality with excess liquidity feeding exuberance; shorts expected a fall but Nifty rose ~95 points and Bank Nifty 500+ the next session. Teaches confirmation bias: traders interpret news to fit their positions; markets do not obey officials.
lessons: Confirmation bias: longs notice only bullish news, shorts only bearish - interpretation of news matters more than the news itself.
Markets are not rational and do not listen to politicians or bureaucrats; traders must follow the market's direction, not the commentary.
quotes: Markets are not rational. Markets don't listen to politicians or bureaucrats. The market has its own mind.

summary: Q&A episode: futures don't receive dividends but need lower margin for covered calls - buy cash only in dividend months; futures long + sold calls = covered-call income on dividend stocks. Trading-ban handling (reduce only, prefer large caps). Strike availability timeline (3 monthly + 10 weekly + long-dated). Portfolio-level stop loss (2% of capital) over per-trade stops. Deep/debt-fund-vs-FD and Japan's lost-decades questions.
lessons: Futures positions don't earn dividends but need only exposure margin for covered calls - hold futures normally, switch to cash in dividend-declaration months.
Set a portfolio-level stop (e.g. 2% of total capital across all positions) instead of mechanical per-trade stop losses.

strategies.name: Dividend-cycle futures + covered call
strategies.construction: Long futures on dividend-paying stock most of the year (cheap covered-call margin); switch to cash market only in dividend months
strategies.best_regime: High-dividend-yield large caps with liquid options
strategies.adjustments: Time cash/futures switch to the dividend record period
strategies.risks: Futures basis/discount eats part of the dividend benefit

quotes: Small people look for opportunity. Big people create opportunity.
